I can't watch the video because my work network won't allow it, but I feel oddly compelled to correct the use of the phrase "bum rush" in the title.

"Bum rush" is when you rudely grab someone by the collar or elbow and quickly escort them out of view. The term comes from restaurants and saloons (mostly in the wild west) when you wanted an undesirable customer tossed out - you'd bum rush them out the door (rush the bum out!). Would apply to a lower-class customer in a fancy restaurant being asked to leave, or if you show up at your new girlfriend's family party unexpectedly and she gets embarrassed and asks you to leave.

Somehow recently the phrase has come to mean being swarmed by a pack or forcefully pushing your way through -- the bum doing the rushing in -- but it really means rushing the bum OUT!

Just my 2 cents. And yes, I realize English is a living language.
